summary: Vanadium offers strong baseline privacy by stripping out Google tracking while prioritizing top-tier security hardening, though it lacks built-in ad blocking and advanced anti-fingerprinting tools.

strengths.description: Built from Chromium with Google services, crash reporting, and telemetry completely removed.
Disables peer-to-peer WebRTC by default (forcing proxied connections) and blocks websites from accessing local network interfaces, preventing sites from exposing your real IP address.
Uses DuckDuckGo as the default search engine instead of Google.
Uses strict sandboxing, memory protections, and rapid Chromium security patches to stop malicious websites from compromising your device.

limitations_and_tradeoffs.limitation: No built-in ad or tracker blocking
limitations_and_tradeoffs.description: Does not include an integrated ad blocker or support browser extensions; requires network-level filtering like NextDNS, RethinkDNS, or a VPN with DNS blocking.
Does not aggressively randomize or spoof browser fingerprints, as doing so can weaken Chromium's security boundaries.
Enabling optional 'Standard' or 'Enhanced' Safe Browsing features can send URLs and page data to Google for analysis.

recommendations.everyday_browsing: Vanadium paired with a private DNS service
recommendations.out_of_the_box_ad_blocking: Brave (note: slightly increases device attack surface)
